name: Can pool removal be done on a hillside property in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What extra issues come up when a pool is on a slope or near a retaining wall?
mainEntity.text: What extra issues come up when a pool is on a slope or near a retaining wall?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hillside pool removal is possible, but the site conditions make it much more technical. Sloped lots can require extra attention to access, equipment staging, erosion control, drainage redirection, and retaining-wall protection. Removing a pool can change how water moves across the property, so the finished grade must be planned carefully to avoid washout or pressure against walls. In some cases, the contractor may need to use smaller equipment or a more manual process because large machinery cannot safely reach the backyard. Homeowners should ask whether the contractor has worked on hillside sites and whether the bid includes stabilization measures. Because these projects can affect nearby structures and drainage patterns, a site visit is usually essential before any realistic estimate is given. The final goal is not just to remove the pool, but to leave the slope stable and usable.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but hillside pool removal is more complex because of drainage, soil stability, access, and retaining-wall protection. These sites often need more careful grading and compaction to prevent erosion, settlement, or damage to nearby structures.
